title: Projection adapters and incremental stream shims for typed Python SDK responses
creator: Maya Chen
description: Proposal and implementation work for a new Response Projection and Stream Shim layer in the Python SDK. The goal is to provide a low-latency, incremental binding API that can map streaming LLM output into typed Pydantic/dataclass models while supporting: resumable retries, checkpointing for long-lived streams, schema evolution across model versions, and ergonomic fallbacks for existing callback-based usages. This ticket covers design, prototype, API signals, compatibility shims, and the first integration tests and examples.
acceptance_criteria: Define a minimal public API for incremental projections (ResponseProjection) that can be used as an async iterator and as a synchronous convenience wrapper.
Implement a StreamShim that transforms raw token/partial JSON chunks into projected model instances with best-effort partial validation.
Support a checkpoint token mechanism so the client can request resume from the last durable checkpoint after a transient failure.
Provide a compatibility layer that exposes the new projection as a drop-in replacement for the existing on_event callback pattern.
Add integration tests covering: partial-object assembly, retry+resume behavior, schema evolution where fields are added/renamed, and backpressure scenarios with large streams.
Publish a short examples doc (notebook + README) demonstrating pydantic and dataclass usage patterns and migration notes.
Performance: projection layer introduces <5ms median added latency per message on typical dev workloads and no >5% throughput regression in batching benchmarks.
tasks: Design API sketch and compatibility surface for ResponseProjection (doc + proto code)
Prototype StreamShim that consumes generator of token/chunk events and yields partial/complete model instances
Implement checkpointing contract: checkpoint token format, durable flush points, and SDK helpers
Add retry/resume logic in python sdk transport to accept a checkpoint token and resume stream from server
Write unit tests for partial reconstruction and schema evolution scenarios
Add integration tests with runtime using local runtime simulator and fixture model responses
Author migration guide and example notebooks (pydantic and dataclass examples)
Benchmark end-to-end performance and update optimize guide with recommended knobs
Open PR with implementation and request design review from eng infra and SDK leads
risks_and_tradeoffs: Evolving schema: full validation on partial streaming data can be expensive; choose best-effort partial validation plus final strict validation on completion
Checkpoint granularity: more frequent checkpoints improve resume semantics but increase metadata overhead; default to event boundaries for efficiency
Compatibility: adding a new abstraction risks fragmentation; provide clear migration path and wrapper utilities for callbacks
Backpressure: yielding heavy model instances could slow streaming; provide lightweight projection mode that returns only delta fields until completion

Retries semantics: server-side resume support required for robust resumption. Without server support, client fallback will re-request and reassemble from last token which may affect idempotency guarantees
implementation_notes: New types: ResponseProjection (async iterator + sync wrapper), ProjectionCursor (checkpoint token string), StreamShim (adapter from raw stream to projection). Keep all classes thin and composable.

Pydantic usage: allow create_model and parse_obj for final validation. During streaming, emit Pydantic models in "partial=True" mode storing missing fields as None and attach metadata ._projection_state
Dataclasses usage: generate lightweight builder objects with typed attrs and a finalize() method that runs final validation using a small runtime validator plugin
Transport changes: add optional resume_with_checkpoint(checkpoint: str) option to streaming client. Server integration tests should include a mock that honors checkpoint tokens.

Performance: avoid copying token buffers for each projection invocation; reuse a streaming buffer and yield views where possible. Use C-accelerated JSON incremental parser if available (oruvia/ijson fallback).
Docs: add examples/typed_streams.ipynb and a README migration guide showing old callback -> new projection migration with before/after snippets
